summary:
Silent Sentinels is an interactive, voice-narrated digital web museum designed for school-age space enthusiasts to explore NASA's historic hardware and discarded equipment resting across the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

To address the challenge (*Abandoned but not Forgotten*), the app transforms dense technical records from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) into engaging, first-person narratives where historic spacecraft—such as the Apollo 11 Eagle descent stage, the Opportunity rover, and Pioneer 10—tell their own stories. It includes filterable celestial zones, built-in text-to-speech audio narration for accessibility, and an interactive knowledge quiz.

This project is important because while active missions make daily headlines, these silent sentinels are vital monuments to human ingenuity. By making space history imaginative, accessible, and scientifically accurate, Silent Sentinels inspires the next generation of students to connect with humanity's cosmic heritage and understand the foundational science that made modern exploration possible.
details:
Silent Sentinels of the Solar System is an interactive, voice-narrated web application designed to bring NASA's historic, retired hardware resting across the Moon, Mars, and deep space back to life. Instead of presenting dense technical tables or dry archive text, the app uses a first-person storytelling approach where each spacecraft or lander—such as the Apollo 11 Eagle descent stage, the Opportunity rover, and Pioneer 10—shares its own mission journey, engineering challenges, and scientific discoveries. Users can filter artifacts by celestial zone (Moon, Mars, or Deep Space), inspect authentic NSSDCA telemetry (coordinates, active spans, and status), trigger built-in audio narration, and test their knowledge with an interactive junior space historian quiz.

Benefits:
The app bridges the gap between complex space science and young learners. By transforming raw historical data into personal narratives, it eliminates the intimidation factor of traditional archives, making space history fun, memorable, and accessible to students, educators, and casual space enthusiasts of all ages.

Intended Impact:
Our goal is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers. By highlighting the silent monuments left behind by humanity, we foster a deep personal connection to our cosmic heritage and demonstrate how foundational past missions enable modern space exploration.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

Frontend & UI: Semantic HTML5, Modern CSS3 (Responsive Grid, Glassmorphism UI)

Logic & Audio Accessibility: Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Web Speech API (speechSynthesis for zero-dependency text-to-speech audio narration)

Data & Hosting: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) for authentic mission telemetry, hosted via GitHub Pages / Netlify.

Creativity of the Project:
Rather than building a standard database search tool, we reimagined space artifacts as active storytellers. Giving a voice to dormant machines like "Oppy" the rover or the Apollo 11 descent stage creates an emotional and immersive educational experience that standard textbooks cannot match.

Factors Our Team Considered:
Target Audience: We intentionally designed the tone, vocabulary, and UI to appeal directly to school-age space enthusiasts.

Accessibility: We integrated a one-click text-to-speech audio reader so users with reading difficulties or visual preferences can listen to the stories aloud.

Scientific Accuracy: All coordinates, NSSDCA catalog IDs, and scientific outcomes were rigorously cross-referenced to ensure absolute fidelity to official NASA records.
